nodes.summary: If a real formal power series $f$ has positive log-convex coefficients, then the coefficient of $X^n$ in $f$ is strictly positive for every natural number $n$.
nodes.title: Coefficients of a positive log-convex series are positive

nodes.summary: A real formal power series $f = \sum_n a_n X^n$ has positive log-convex coefficients if $a_n > 0$ for every natural number $n$ and $a_{n+1}^2 \le a_n a_{n+2}$ for every natural number $n$. This is the hypothesis of Kaluza's bounds for the coefficients of the reciprocal series.
nodes.title: Positive log-convex coefficients

nodes.summary: Let $f = \sum_n a_n X^n$ be a real formal power series with positive log-convex coefficients, and let $f^{-1} = \sum_n b_n X^n$ be its reciprocal in the ring of formal power series. Then $b_0 = a_0^{-1}$, $b_0 > 0$, and $-a_n / a_0^2 \le b_n \le 0$ for every $n \ge 1$.
nodes.title: Kaluza's bounds for the coefficients of a reciprocal power series

nodes.summary: If a real formal power series $f = \sum_n a_n X^n$ has positive log-convex coefficients, then $a_{n+1}^2 \le a_n a_{n+2}$ for every natural number $n$.
nodes.title: Log-convexity of the coefficients
